column3: The Hebrew says “He incited”; NASB renders “it incited,” taking the anger as subject.
“Enroll” is rendered “register.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“South of the city” is rendered “on the right side of the city,” and “wadi” as “valley.”
NASB keeps the obscure names “Tahtim-hodshi” and “Dan-jaan”; the Hebrew is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Men of strength” is rendered “valiant men.”
“David’s heart struck him” is rendered “David’s heart troubled him.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Laying on you” is rendered “offering you.”
The Hebrew reads “seven years of famine” (1 Chr 21:12 has “three”); NASB follows the Hebrew.
“Compassions” is rendered “mercies.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“The angel the destroyer among the people” is rendered “the angel who destroyed the people,” and “let drop” as “relax.”
NASB does not have “the shepherd” (a Septuagint addition); NASB adds “it is I who.”
“Raise up” is rendered “erect.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Bowed down” is rendered “bowed his face … before the king.”
Close to the Hebrew; “restrained” is rendered “held back.”
“Equipment of the oxen” is rendered “yokes of the oxen.”
The Hebrew “everything gives Araunah, O king, to the king” is difficult; NASB keeps it close.
“Without paying” is rendered “which cost me nothing.”
“Was entreated” is rendered “was moved by entreaty.”
